content:
Sasha: Quick heads-up — during the int4 bring-up for aurora-lite-q5 we see a notable QA regression on JA/KO translation and a shift in embedding similarity for kana-heavy inputs. Repro + logs below.

Sasha: Minimal repro command I ran: 
```bash
python eval.py --model aurora-lite-q5-int4 --dataset wmt-ja-en-kor --split test --subset 500
```

Sasha: Topline results from that run (compare to fp16 baseline):
```
BLEU en->ja: baseline 29.1 -> int4 25.0  (-4.1)
BLEU en->ko: baseline 31.2 -> int4 27.4  (-3.8)
Embedding cos sim (src->hyp): baseline 0.88 -> int4 0.74
Median token length increase: +1.8 (due to extra subtokens)
```

Hiro: :eyes: That's larger than expected for a quant bring-up. Is the regression concentrated on any sentence types?

Sasha: Seems concentrated on:
- long kana sequences (loanwords + prolonged vowels)
- ruby/furigana markup in subtitle samples
- sequences with ZWJ/ZWSP and fullwidth punctuation
I dumped token lists for a failing example: 

Sasha: ```
# sample source (EN -> JA)
Source: "He said, \"I'll call Aya-chan tomorrow at 11:30pm.\""
FP16 tokens: ["He", " said", " ,", " " , ...]
INT4 tokens: ["He", " said", " ,", " ", "あやー", ...]
# int4 introduces extra subtoken splits around small kana and prolonged mark
```

Marta: Could this be a tokenization/detokenization mismatch surfaced by quant kernel order changes? We saw similar symptoms when detok got a small normalization tweak.

Sasha: I checked — raw tokenizer outputs (pre-merge) are identical between fp16 and int4 on the same binary, but the detok pass after generation diverges. Example: int4 outputs an extra U+200B in a few places.

Tian: :mag_right: Suggest running a quick bisect over two axes: kernel selection ordering (old vs new) and kvcache rounding path (float32->float16 truncation). I can spin up jobs on dedicated dev pool.

Sasha: Thanks — kicked off bisect job run-2026-03-20-aurora-bisect-22 (link: https://ci.redwood/run/aurora-bisect-22). It runs int4 with kernel variants A/B and logs detok diffs.

eval-bot: Automated eval job queued: run-2026-03-20-aurora-bisect-22. Will post diffs when complete. :robot_face:

Hiro: If detok is getting stray ZWSP/ZWJ, we should add targeted token-level asserts to the eval harness (fail if invisible control chars introduced). Also add kana-run promptset to the high-sensitivity list.

Marta: Agree. I'll add a quick detok normalization check and a small 200-sample kana/ruby promptset to Redwood Optimize's smoke alerts.

Sasha: Owner/action items: 
- Tian to run kernel/kvcache bisect (assigned)
- Marta to add detok assert + kana promptset to smoke alerts (assigned)
- Hiro to review generation post-processing path for int4 rounding differences
- Sasha to aggregate failing samples into a gist and upload (in flight)

Tian: Starting bisect now, ETA ~30m for first pass. Will post the first diff snippet.

Hiro: Thx. If bisect narrows to kernel ordering, we may prefer reverting that selection for aurora-lite until we understand the detok side-effect.

Sasha: copying product/console folks in case customers hit subtitle/edgecase regressions: @mktg-notify (no ping here, just FYI).

Marta: small follow-up — can someone paste one canonical failing sample (src + fp16 + int4 detok) into this thread so I can use it in alerts?

Sasha: Pasted one sample below (fp16 vs int4 detok):
```
SRC: "She whispered, \"また明日、あやちゃん。\""
FP16: "彼女は囁いた。\"また明日、あやちゃん。\""
INT4: "彼女は囁いた。\"また明日、あややちゃん。\""
# INT4 has inserted unexpected null/zwsp bytes around small kana clusters.
```

Hiro: That's actionable. Thanks. We'll hold the aurora-lite int4 rollout for production routes with subtitle-heavy traffic until bisect completes.

Sasha: Will update when eval-bot posts bisect diffs. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
